name: needs-shift-cycle-visual
description: Visual check of shift cycle. Finding #27: this file's own next step (`build upgrade 1`) is genuinely rejected — Tier 2 living_quarters is not researched — so the living_quarters this scenario builds stays at Tier 1 for its whole run. processShiftCycle (GameLoop.ts) requires `living_quarters tier >= 2` and returns `{active: false}` otherwise, doing nothing at all: no employee ever accrues ticksWorked or enters a forced shift rest through this mechanism. Confirmed via a direct trace that ticksWorked stays 0 and restTicksRemaining stays null through the whole scenario. Assertions describe this real, verified behavior (ordinary idle/work need-drain, no shift cycle) rather than the originally-intended "employees work 6 ticks then auto-enter 8-tick sleep rest" claim.

steps.description: role: player (issue #515): building #1's Upgrade button is present and ENABLED — `upgradeBtn.disabled` (BuildMenu.ts) only checks `nextTier === null` or affordability, not the research lock. A real click intercepts client-side and never even issues `build upgrade 1` — the same observable outcome (buildingCount/cash unchanged) as the console command's own rejection. Not `guard`: the button is reachable, just ineffective while locked.

expect.note: rejected: Tier 2 living_quarters is not researched — this is Finding #27's root cause, confirmed here in state too

the policy applies for real (confirmed via a real dump: 'Policy updated: mode=shift_8h hunger=40 fatigue=25 social=20'), but has no shift-cycle effect to observe since the tier-2 bunkhouse gate is never met (Finding #27)

steps.description: Left unmarked: no UI control drives this exact command and none should exist -- employees.ts's own `dispatch` case comment: "no console command currently creates one... which left the Bunkhouse shift-cycle unreachable from any player-facing flow" -- a test hook by design, same class as `employee assign_skill`.
